newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares slip, seen volatile.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares slip, seen volatile.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 1.79 percent on Tuesday on what traders attributed to profit-taking after recent gains and forecast that the market would remain volatile over the short term.
The 11-share SBI index fell 26.3 points to 1,441.1, reversing a two-day surge when the blue-chip index notched up gains of 13.2 percent.

"Traders were probably selling to cash in profits, or in fear that the market may be headed for a downturn. There will be some uncertainty on the market until fresh news concerning foreign investment becomes available," Franci Zmavc, a trader at brokerage Intara said.
Last week the Bank of Slovenia said that international investors would have to open special custody accounts at one of the country's 14 fully licenced banks in order to trade in Slovenian securities.
The bank later defended its move, saying it was purely so that it could regulate foreign portfolio investment.
Overall 13 shares fell, two rose and one was unchanged, while another nine were untraded. Turnover fell to 442.3 million tolars from 484.3 million.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 6.07 percent to 58,000 tolars on volume of 2,765 shares for total turnover of 169.5 million tolars.
Warehousing company BTC led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.82 percent to 13,230 tolars on volume of 713 shares for total turnover of 9.8 million.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the biggest gainer, rising 3.13 percent to 16,500 tolars on volume of 950 shares for total turnover of 15.7 million.
